beowulf-fitt-22 cruces and guesses (drafter)
1478-79 forðgewitenum on fæder stǣle: dative participle agreeing with mē; "departed" = dead (grammar certain, euphemism read from context).
1484-87 brēac þonne mōste: object of brēac unstated; "enjoyed him" is a guess.
1489-90 ealde lāfe / wǣgsweord / heardecg: wǣgsweord "wave-sword" guess (editors wīg-, wæl-); which sword is the heirloom (Hrunting itself?) not stated; heardecg taken as adjective on the sword.
1492 Weder-: "Weder" in Weder-Gēata taken as "weather/storm" without certainty (l keeps "Weder-Geats").
1495 hwīl dæges: length of the dive ("a good part of a day") a guess.
1498 heorogīfre: "fierce-greedy" (heoro- as intensifier) a guess; alt "sword-greedy".
1498 hund missēra: 50 or 100 years undecided; l "a hundred half-years".
1497 sē ðe: masculine forms for Grendel's mother (cf. 1392).
1508 hē þǣm mōdig wæs: þǣm disputed (MS þæm; editors þæs, þēah, þǣr); rendered "brave as he was".
1510 swe[n]cte: MS swecte; Kemble's emendation to swencan.
1511 bræc "broke at" (mail holds): sense guessed.
1513 [in] nīðsele: Thorkelin's addition; wæter nǣnig variants in apparatus.
1518 grundwyrgenne: "ground-accursed one" guess (wyrgen fem. of wearg-type word).
1520 hond sweng ne oftēah: MS hord swenge, emended; sense follows Klaeber's text.
1543 oferwearp: no object; read as reflexive "overthrew [himself] / stumbled"; alt. editors supply [hine]. Real crux.
1546 brūnecg: "brown-edged" ("burnished"?) guess; [ond] added by Grundtvig.
1537 be eaxle: editors read feaxe "hair"; Klaeber's eaxle kept.
1550 forsīðod: "perished" from forsīðian, read from lexicon, moderately sure.
